714.2. An effect whose source has left play has the attributes its source had when it left, including attributes shared with it by its column then. See rule 704.7a.

Example: Bellowing Boulder dies with a Deadly unit beside it and its ping on the stack; the ping is still Deadly.

720. Modifications, General

720.1. A modification (mod) changes a card's abilities by combining cards together. A card that can be a mod carries one of two mod symbols: the augment symbol (721) or the graft symbol (722). See rules 721, 722, 305.

Example: Aetherflux Golem (augment) and Flame Juggle (graft) are offered as mods; The Foretold, with neither symbol, is not.

720.2a A timing icon other than Virus does not change when a card can be applied as a mod. A Battle card cannot be applied as a mod during battle, except under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5) or to a Modular card as it is played (724). See rules 207.6, 723.5, 724, 720.2b.

Example: Burning Vengeance, a Battle card, is not offered as a mod during battle, but it is offered to Spellbind, a Modular card, played in battle.

Example: Hooba-Lin, a Haste augment card, cannot be applied as a mod in the haste step when no card such as Slurpr allows it.

720.2b A mod can be applied outside deployment only where a rule or a card says so: a Virus during battle (723.2); a card augmented in battle under a card that lets it be augmented as if it were a Virus, such as Rook (723.5); a mod applied in the haste step under a card that allows it, such as Slurpr (504.8a); and a mod applied to a Modular card as it is played (724). No other card widens the window. See rules 723, 504.8a, 724.

720.3. Applying a mod is not playing a card, from whatever zone the mod comes. An ability that triggers when a player plays a unit, a spell or a card does not trigger when a mod is applied. See rules 701.2, 701.2a.

Example: Stalwart Sentinel counts a spell played from the bin, but not a mod applied from the bin.

Example: A Virus applied during battle is not a spell: Origon does not negate it, and it does not count as a spell played.

722.4f A composite fizzles when it has lost all of its targets, and then none of it happens, its untargeted parts included. While at least one target remains, every part resolves as far as it can. Only a composite that was never targeted cannot fizzle: one with no part that calls for a target, or one whose only target was optional ("up to one") and none was chosen (see rule 704.6g). See rule 704.

Example: Spewing Mushroom carries Biotoxicity and Technological Superiority as grafts. It attacks, and its composite trigger targets Spewing Mushroom, the only target it declares. The opponent deletes the Mushroom with Leaping Lillik in response: the composite fizzles, and Biotoxicity's untargeted Poisons are not created either.

723.1. Virus is a timing icon. A Virus card can be applied as an augment from the hand during battle, as well as being played and augmented normally during deployment. See rule 207.5.

Example: Aetherflux Golem augments the attacker from hand during battle; in deployment it may be played as a unit or augmented.

723.2b A Virus in a bin cannot be applied during battle by its Virus ability. From the bin it can be applied as an ordinary mod during deployment, and outside deployment only where another card opens a window: augmenting in battle under a card such as Rook (723.5), applying to a Modular card as it is played (724), or applying in the haste step under a card such as Slurpr (504.8a). See rules 405.8a, 723.5, 724, 504.8a, 720.2b.

Example: Bumblecrab, a Virus, is offered from the hand in battle but not from the bin; in deployment it is offered from the bin.

Example: With a Rook in the battle's region, a card is augmented out of the bin during battle.

Example: Pull Under deletes an enemy unit and puts it into the caster's bin: the caster trashes it.

801.13. "Exchange" is printed in four senses, each read from its card: exchanging a unit in play for a unit card in a bin (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph), exchanging control of two units (Organic Exchange), exchanging control of a unit for a spell another player played (Hexbane Shiitake), and exchanging the base stats of two units (Body Swap). See rules 711, 106.8.

802.1m When Tough and Balanced both apply to a unit, they apply one after the other, from top to bottom. If Tough is augmented onto a Balanced unit, or a Tough unit attacks with a Balanced unit behind it, the unit has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. If Tough is applied to a Balanced unit, it has its stats balanced, then its defense doubled. The attributes a unit has from its augments apply first, in the order the mods were attached, the first attached first Digital client; then its printed attributes; then those effects have given it; then those shared from its column, front to back. An attribute the unit has from more than one source takes the position of the first. See rules 206.4, 721.

Example: A 3/1 augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) and then Child of Aether (Balanced) is a 3/3; augmented in the other order it is a 3/6.

Example: Child of Aether prints Balanced and is a 2/0. Augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough), its defense is doubled (still 2/0), then its stats balanced: it is a 2/2.

Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) attacks with Child of Aether (Balanced) behind it: its defense is doubled (0/8), then its stats balanced, and it is an 8/8.

Example: Child of Aether given Tough by an effect is balanced first (2/2), then its defense doubled: a 2/4.

802.1n A Pure card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all its other attributes in that interaction (see rule 802.25). This includes the attributes that change stats: in an interaction with a Pure card, Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply. A column striking a player with a Pure card in it ignores its other attributes too (see rule 802.25b). See rule 802.25.

Example: Rampart Guardian (a 0/4 with Tough) is dealt 5 damage by a Pure source. In that interaction it ignores Tough, so its defense is 4 and it dies.

Example: A Balanced 4/1 dealt 3 by a Pure source dies: Balanced does not apply in that pairing.

Example: An Unaware source dealing 3 damage to a Pure unit pumped from 2/3 to 4/5 does not read it at its printed 2/3: it survives, where a pumped non-Pure 2/3 dies.

Example: An unblocked Pure column strikes in the normal sub-step and does not double or draw.

802.8a Inverted inverts the net change to a unit's stats. An Inverted unit's power is its base power minus the net change to its power, and its defense is its base defense minus the net change to its defense. It is worked out on the total change, not on each change separately. See rule 206.4.

Example: Malformed Monstrosity (10/9) with its -7/-7, in a column with Reality Bender, is a 17/16.

802.16. Piercing. Piercing is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Excess damage from piercing sources is dealt to the recipient's controller." See rules 802.1, 608.

802.16a Excess damage, for Piercing, is the damage a source deals to a unit beyond that unit's lethal damage. A unit's lethal damage is worked out after Powerful has doubled the source's damage; it is reduced for a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt double what reaches it; it is 1 if the source has Deadly; and damage already dealt to the unit counts towards it, including damage dealt to it earlier by the same effect (see rule 608.6e). See rules 608.6e, 802.3, 802.10, 802.11.

Example: A Powerful Piercing source deals 3 to a 1/1. The 3 is doubled to 6; 1 is lethal; 5 is excess.

Example: A 10-power Piercing column is blocked by a Vulnerable 3/8. Lethal damage is 4, which is dealt as 8; the other 6 is excess.

Example: One effect names the same unit twice with Piercing. The unit is given its lethal damage once, and the rest of both hits is excess.

802.25. Pure. Pure is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes." See rule 802.1.

Sources and verification
PrintedConfirmedverified in round 1 · verifier ran 1 test, passed · 1 gate test file
  • Printed card: Just a Unit: (Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes.)
  • Our glossary (not a source) glossary: Pure: Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes.
  • Tests 40-light-c.test.ts
  • Demonstrated by test 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: the exchange is attribute-blind in BOTH directions
  • Key attr.pure

802.25a A Pure card ignores its own other attributes too. Its own stat-changing attributes, Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware, do not apply to it at any time, whether or not it is in an interaction. Nor do its other attributes apply when its column strikes a player: an unblocked Pure column has no Swift, Sluggish, Powerful, Thieving, Lethal or Blessed. See rule 802.12.

Example: An Alluring column that is itself Pure ignores its own Alluring and never triggers.

Example: A Pure unit that is also Feeble can block.

Example: A Pure Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) that is in no interaction reads 0/4.

Example: A Pure Child of Aether (2/0, Balanced) ignores its own Balanced, reads 2/0 and dies in the state check.

Example: A Pure Bubb ignores its own Unaware, so the counters on it count.

Example: An unblocked Pure column strikes in the normal sub-step and does not double or draw.

803. Other Keyword Abilities

803.1. Some keywords are not combat attributes. Burst and Unstable are printed in purple text and are called non-combat attributes: they describe a card, and generally have nothing to do with combat. The other keywords in this section (Haste, Battle, [once], Ambush and Prophecy) are timing marks, limits and ways to play a card. See rules 802, 720, 204.5.

Example: A modded Chitin Shredder attacks in a column with a vanilla unit: the vanilla unit shares its Powerful, but it does not become Unstable.

803.6h An Ambush on the stack is not a spell effect: the card played as an Ambush is a unit, not a spell. An effect that targets, negates or recalls spell effects cannot affect it, but one that names an effect, or a nonspell effect, can. A negated Ambush puts its ambushing card into the bin. See rules 700.1a, 704.4a.

Example: Nothyr ("negate up to one target nonspell effect") can target an Ambush on the stack and negate it; the ambushing card goes to the bin.

Example: Void Mandible negates an Ambush on the stack: the ambusher never takes the slot and its target is not recalled.

Example: Dreadwave Devourer, which negates a target spell effect, cannot target an Ambush on the stack, and the Ambush resolves.

Example: Cosmic Reversal ("Recall all other spell effects and spell units") recalls a spell on the stack and leaves an Ambush beside it, which then resolves.

803.7m A condition that counts units dying, such as Vengeance's "13 Units Die", counts only the deaths its controller witnessed: deaths in a region where that player was present. A player is present in their own region, and in an enemy region once they have attacked into it, until regroup. See rules 601, 604.3a.

Example: A player attacks into the opponent's region with a unit, so both players are present there. Two of the opponent's units die in that region: each player counts two deaths toward "Units Die".

901.5b For state checks the draw of 4 and the put-back of 2 are one step: a player's units are not checked for death while that player still has 2 cards to put back, so they are judged on the hand that remains. See rules 503, 713.

Example: Dreadspawn Horror with 1 card in hand: drawing 4 does not kill it, and after the put-back it is a 4/2.

Example: With 3 cards in hand, Dreadspawn Horror's controller draws 4 and puts 2 back, keeping 5 cards: the Horror then dies.

Engine-only rules (awaiting the owner's sign-off)

  • 103.3b In constructed, each player's opening hand is 4 cards. No source gives the constructed opening hand; it is the client's convention.
  • 109.9n A bounded "When I am trashed" ability is limited for each trashed card, not for each player and card name: two copies of one card trashed in the same turn each trigger.
  • 111.3a A cost that removes counters from the player's allies, or recalls an ally, likewise uses only the player's own units in the region where the cost is paid.
  • 406.4b A self-erasing spell that is negated or fails to resolve goes to the bin. Its "Erase me" never happened.
  • 603.1c Two side-blocking units may stand in the same side-block column, one in its front slot and one in its back slot.
  • 713.3a Deaths are also checked while an effect is still resolving, not only at safe points. Each time an effect puts counters on a unit, and after each part of an effect made of several parts, units that should be dead die at once, before the rest of the effect happens.
  • 723.4e Triggered and activated abilities, Viruses, units being cast and Ambushes on the stack are not legal hosts for a Virus.
  • D1.2i When a player chooses the order of replacement effects (see rule 708.4a), each choice is the unit whose effect it is: the player answers by clicking that unit on the board, the choices are not also buttons in the prompt bar, and the prompt says what is being chosen. A question raised by combat damage or by rot is asked before any of that damage or rot is dealt. The other player sees that a question is open, but not the question; while the rot question is open at the start of deployment, the other player cannot deploy.
  • D2.3 A player may turn on auto-pass. With it on, the client passes priority for the player only in a window where passing is the only thing they could do. Auto-pass never passes through an open decision.
  • D3.1 A game may be played with a chess clock, in which each player has a bank of time. The home screen offers three settings: no clock, 45 minutes and 60 minutes.
  • D3.1a Unless the player chooses otherwise, the bank is 45 minutes for a constructed game and 60 minutes for a live draft.
  • D3.1b A game with no clock shows no clocks.
  • D3.1c Choosing a clock setting does not make a game a custom game.
  • D3.1d A player's clock is shown as critical when it is down to a tenth of the game's bank or to one minute, whichever is less.
  • D3.2 A player's clock runs only while the game is waiting on that player, and only while both players are connected. Neither clock runs while a proposed fix waits for its answer (see rule D4.5e).
  • D3.2a In a step both players take at once, both clocks run; a player's clock stops when that player finishes the step.
  • D3.2b A player's clock does not run in a priority window that their standing pass is answering, and the other player, who has nothing to do there, is not billed either. A real choice is billed even while a standing pass is set. If the client's pass has not arrived within a short backstop, the server passes for the player, and that pass is logged like any other. While a proposed fix waits for its answer, the server does not pass for a standing pass.
  • D3.2c A player watching a recap is off the clock until the playback ends or the server's hold on it lapses. Acting ends the hold.
  • D3.3 A player whose clock runs out loses the game, and the log says they ran out of time. This happens even if neither player acts.
  • D3.4 A game is closed when nobody has moved in it for an hour, if fewer than five actions have been taken, or for twelve hours otherwise, and nobody (no player and no watcher) has been connected to it for the five-minute reconnect grace. An open tab keeps an idle game open.
  • D3.4a A connected player or a watcher keeps an idle game open, and an empty game is given a grace period for a player to reconnect.
  • D3.4b A game closed for being idle has no winner, is not rated, and is recorded as unfinished.
  • D4.1a The opponent acting in the same step does not stop a player's undo.
  • D4.1b An undo cannot go back past what the step itself did as it began, such as a payment or an ability that happens at the start of the step. A player's own undo, in any step, never takes back an agreed edit (see rule D4.5), and takes back an action from before one only if the edit would mean exactly the same afterwards. It never goes back past the point an agreed rewind returned the game to: only another agreed rewind can.
  • D4.5a An edit is one of: setting a player's life total, to a whole number from 1 to 999; a player drawing from 1 to 10 cards off the top of their deck; moving one of the proposer's own cards from their hand, bin or cache to their hand, bin or cache, or to the top or bottom of their deck; or taking a unit off the board to its controller's hand, bin or the bottom of their deck. A token taken off the board is simply gone.
  • D4.5b An edit is quiet: nothing triggers on it. A unit it takes off the board neither dies nor despawns, a card it puts into a bin is not trashed, a card it takes out of a bin does not count as leaving the bin, and the cards it draws are not a draw for anything that listens for one.
  • D4.5c An agreed edit may be made in any step, the hidden planning, haste and deploy steps included, except while a decision is open for either player; it is shown to both players at once. A rewind may be proposed at any time.
  • D4.5e A proposal states the fix and the proposer's reason, which is required. It lapses after 60 seconds, or as soon as any action lands, and the proposer may withdraw it. Only the other player can accept it; after a decline the proposer must wait 15 seconds before proposing again. The proposer's reason is filed as a bug report. Fixes made one after another, with no game action between them, are one run and file one report, with every fix's reason in order; the run is filed when it ends, for instance when the next game action lands, and a server restart before then does not lose it.
  • D5.1a The recap changes nothing in the game. A game played with recap frames is the same game, action for action, as one without them.
  • D5.1b A frame of the opponent's move shows that move on their side, their hand still face down, and the player's own side as the player left it.
  • D5.1c A move with nothing to show is not given a frame, but its log line is kept.
  • D5.1d The end of turn is played as one frame per trigger, in order.
  • D5.1f Undoing a move inside the step removes that move's frame and keeps the others.
  • D5.3 The deployment recap pauses after the opponent's moves and again after the end of turn; the haste step's recap pauses the same way. Skip jumps to the next pause, never past it. A quiet end of turn does not pause twice.
  • D5.3b The hand-over to the next turn at the end of a recap pauses longer than a frame. Every recap, live, watched again or in Learn to Play, is paced by the same rule.
  • D5.5c During a recap playback, skipping does not jump to the live state. Skip (the S key, Space, or the Skip button drawn on the play bar) jumps to the next stop, and on a stop it continues the playback.
  • D6.2e A card that reveals cards from the deck without the Glimpse keyword, such as Tides of the Cosmos or Big Glimpse Card, shows the revealed cards to every player as cards, in the notice a glimpse uses. A player whose own open question already shows those cards is not shown the notice. Inside a hidden step the reveal is held for the reveal at the end of the step, as a glimpse is.
  • D6.9f A prediction made with Prediction Prophet is shown on that card to both players, as a chip on the card and a line in its text box, from when it is made until the start of deployment reads it. A prediction left from an earlier turn is not shown.
  • D6.9g A triggered ability whose amount is its own column's share of combat damage (Vroot: "When my column deals combat damage, each opponent gains that much life.") shows that share on the stack as its X, the same amount it resolves with, not the total every column dealt.
  • D6.10f In the card zoom, a unit whose attributes are off has only its type bar greyed; a unit whose abilities are off has its text box below the type bar greyed; a unit with both off has both greyed.

Findings: where the engine differs

78 divergences, filed as 127 findings. A divergence that more than one drafting unit found is listed once, under its first id; divergences that share a CT ticket are listed under it.

F-U01-1 Ownership is lost once a stolen card passes through the thief's hand CT-233 rule 102.4 also F-U01-3

Details and evidence

Zones follow control, so a stolen unit that is recalled goes to the thief's hand. The hand holds a bare card name, so when the thief replays it the new unit's owner defaults to the playing seat, and the engine records the thief as owner. The rulings say ownership never moves ("its OWNER's, always, forever"). The verifier's probe measured owner = thief after the replay. Low impact today because zones follow control, but the owner field no longer means what the ruling says it keeps meaning. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

Also found as F-U01-3.

Re-checked: fixed on 2026-10-22 (CT-233): a stolen card keeps its owner through the thief's own hand, bin and cache (551); the routes still open are F-U01-6.

Re-checked (F-U01-3): fixed on 2026-10-22 with F-U01-1 (CT-233): 551 keeps the owner through a hand and a bin.

F-U01-2 The engine lets effects reach the stack and the bins across regions CT-234 rule 101.6 also F-U01-4, F-U01-5

Details and evidence

The rules make the stack, the bins and the caches regional (Manual p.19, Caleb, the owner ruling of 2026-10-11 (“The stack, the bins and the…”)): each region has its own stack, shared by the players present in it, and a player's bin and cache can be reached only where that player is present. The engine keeps one stack for battle and offers a stack item and the cards in either bin as targets from every region, so Frosted Denial, Woodland Warding and Molten Riftbreaker reach across regions. Cache targets already agree (owner ruling of 2026-09-05, “A cached card is a target…”). Unit targeting, statics and triggers are region-scoped and agree with print. (Measured by a verifier probe, not committed, and by the 414 CR test.)

Also found as F-U01-4, F-U01-5.

F-U04-6 "sacrifice me. If you do, …" triggers are sacrificed as a cast cost, against the designer's ruling rule 111.8

F-U08-1 Resource, haste and deployment steps run simultaneously and hidden instead of initiative player first, then non-initiative player CT-247 rules 501.4, 507.3 also F-U09-3

Details and evidence

Print (Manual p.27 legend for 1v1, Rulebook 2023 p.5, Manual p.20) has the initiative player take the resource step and the haste step (and deployment) first and the non-initiative player after, seeing what was done. The engine runs these as hidden simultaneous segments: both seats act at once, interleaved, and the non-initiative player never gets the information print gives them. The verifier measured it: the non-initiative seat activated a resource, finished the resource step and played a haste card before the initiative seat acted. Details and evidence

Print says turns sync up at the end of each step and the draft step is complete once all players have passed their pack. The engine gates the resource step on the acting seat's own draft (and, in constructed, its own recycle of 2) only, so a seat that has committed its draft may activate, recycle and even finish its resource step while the other seat is still drafting. The hidden plan segment keeps the early start out of the other seat's view, so the observable effect may be nil; either sync the step or ratify the early start as a digital convention. F-U10-3 Defending formation adjacency ignores unblocked columns between blockers CT-249 rules 603.2, 606.1f also F-U11-3, F-U11-4

Details and evidence

adjacentInFormation builds the defender grid from the sorted block keys, so blockers on attacking columns 1 and 3 (column 2 unblocked) are treated as left/right neighbours. Inspiration then buffs across the gap (round-1 verifier probe on rule 603.2). The Manual makes blocking position matter for adjacency, and a blocking column is keyed to the attacking column it faces, so the unblocked column is a gap. The engine's own comment calls its reading an approximation. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

F-U23-9 Inside a hidden step a rewind cut may take back the other seat's done-planning flag rule D4.5d

Details and evidence

rewindPlans' ownOnly refuses a cut inside an open hidden step only for the other seat's items marked hidden; donePlanning/doneDeploying/amend are never marked hidden (PUBLIC_IN_HIDDEN), so a cut that takes back the other seat's 'done planning' is offered (probe zz-probe-U23-2b). The code comment says a cut inside the step is offered only where it takes back nothing but the asking seat's own actions. Either the comment/rule should say 'nothing the other seat did unseen', or the cut should be refused. Not a leak (the flag is public), but it does undo the other player's action without it being the step start.

F-U23-10 'Back to the start of the step before' can cut just before a forced action and land at the start of the current step rule D4.5d

Details and evidence

rewindPlans offers 'prev' at startOf(here - 1) without the forced-action check the 'before' cuts get. When the step before began with a forced action (seed 48593: an empty declareBlocks at index 43, step 'battle (blocks, counterattack)'), the cut lands before it, the rebuilt board owes the forced step, and main.ts's drain re-takes it (log back to 44). So the option does not reach the step before, and 485 §4's guarantee 'never a cut at a forced step' fails for this option. The real() check counts items from the cut to the end, which include the current step's actions, so it does not drop a step that was nothing but a forced action, though the 485 §4 CT-340 comment says such a step should not be offered. Shown by client/server/test/zz-probe-U23-1.test.ts 'zz-U23-4'.

F-U24-5 Looking at your own hand tells the other player nothing, not even that a hand was looked at CT-263 rule D6.5a

Details and evidence

The rule says that when an effect lets a player look at a hand, the other players log says only that the hand was looked at. The U24 tester measured Thought Extraction aimed at the caster own hand: the other player log has no look line at all (it goes from Resolving straight to the discard). Aimed at the other player hand, that player log does say "looks at". Four look-at sites skip the public line when the looker owns the hand (if (who !== ctx.controller) g.revealHandTo(...)). Either the rule should say the line is written only when looking at another player hand, or the engine should write it for both. (Measured by a verifier probe; the probe files are not committed.)

Digital-client rules in the main document

100.4, 103.3b, 500.2a, 507.3a, 507.5a, 900.6, 901.7b, 901.8, 901.8a, 901.8b, 901.8c, 902.5, 902.5a, 902.5b, 902.5c, 902.5d, 902.5e, 902.5f, 902.5g, 902.5h. Each is true of this client, not of a game at a table; Annex D holds the rest.

Glossary

Ability
Text on a card that describes the card's effects. See rule 109.1.
Activated ability
An ability written with a colon, whose cost is everything before the colon. See rules 705.1, 109.2.
Active zone
Play or the stack; every other zone is inactive. See rule 400.2.
Adjacent
Next to a unit on its left, right, front or back in the same formation. See rule 603.2.
Affinity
A card's elemental requirement, shown as element pips, and a player's count of non-dormant resources of an element. See rules 105.3, 105.4.
Afflicting
An attribute whose reminder text reads "When an afflicting source kills one or more units, those units' controllers gain a rot." See rule 802.23.
After combat step
The last step of a battle round, a priority window that follows the combat damage step. See rules 609.1, 609.2.
Alluring
An attribute whose reminder text reads "When an alluring column attacks, target enemy can't attack and must block it this combat if able." See rule 802.15.
Ally
A unit under your control in the region where the effect is happening. See rule 102.7.
Ambush
A keyword that lets a unit card be played during battle with the effect "Recall target ally, put me into their position in play." See rule 803.6.
Apply
To put a mod onto a card, a special action that is not playing a card. See rules 720.2, 701.2.
Archenemy
A player setup, typically 2v1, in which the single player takes 1 or 2 turns before the other two begin. See rule 904.12.
Attack step
The first step of a battle, in which the attacking player declares its attacking formation. See rules 505.2, 604.2.
Attack window
The priority window that follows the declaration of an attack, in the region attacked. See rule 605.1.
Attacking
Bringing units, and the spell tokens that travel with them, into a neighbouring enemy region for battle. See rule 604.1.
Attribute
A quality that a card or a token can have, which applies whenever it has it, in combat or not. See rules 802.1, 204.4.
Augment
A modification that adds the text after a card's augment symbol to the card it is applied to. See rules 721.1, 208.1.
Auto-pass
A client preference that passes priority for a player only in a window where passing is the only thing they could do. See rule D2.3.
Balanced
An attribute whose reminder text reads "The power and defense of balanced units are equal to the greater of the two." See rule 802.7.
Banner
The part of a card that offers another way to play it, for a cost of its own, as Ambush and Prophecy do. See rule 203.1.
Battle
A timing keyword: a card with Battle can be played only while its player is in battle with another player. See rules 803.3, 207.4.
Battle phase
The second phase of the turn, and its only interactive one. See rules 505.1, 500.4.
Battle round
One of the two attacks of a 1v1 or team battle phase: the initiative team's attack, then the counterattack. See rule 505.3.
Bin
A player's discard pile. See rule 405.1.
Blessed
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Damage dealt by a blessed source causes its controller to gain that much life." See rule 802.22.
Block step
The second step of a battle, in which the defending player may place its units in front of the attacking formation. See rules 505.2, 606.1.
Block window
The priority window that follows the declaration of blocks. See rule 607.1.
Blocking
How a player who has been attacked defends, by placing units in front of the attacking formation. See rule 606.1.
Bluff haste
A client preference with which the client never finishes the haste step for the player. See rule D2.5b.
Burst
A non-combat attribute printed on spell tokens: casting one casts every spell token of the same name its controller has in that region at the same time. See rule 803.5.
Cache
A public zone of each player's, beside the hand, the bin and the deck; to cache a card is to put it there. See rules 403.1, 801.8.
Card
A physical Algomancy card, one with an Algomancy card back; a token is not a card. See rules 108.1, 304.2.
Cast
To play a spell; casting a spell is playing it. See rule 700.2.
Clock
A chess clock a game may be played with, in which each player has a bank of time. See rule D3.1.
Column
One file of the battle line: the attacking units in it and the defending units placed in front of it. See rule 603.1.
Combat attribute
An attribute printed in gold; units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes. See rules 802.1b, 712.8.
Combat damage
The damage columns deal to each other and to players in the combat damage step. See rule 112.7.
Combat damage step
The step of a battle in which the units in formation deal combat damage. See rule 608.1.
Complexity
What is used to choose which cards are in a game, shown by the colour of the set symbol. See rules 209.2, 209.1.
Concede
To end the game as a loss, in the same way as being eliminated. See rule 104.4.
Conjure (Obsolete)
Not defined by these rules: the old rules glossary's mechanic that created a spell token to be cast at a set time, which no current card prints. See rule 304.11.
Constructed
A game mode in which each player brings their own deck, built before the game, and plays from it. See rule 901.1.
Continuous effect
An effect that changes the game for a period of time rather than once. See rule 709.1.
Controller
The player who controls a card, who may differ from its owner. See rule 102.5.
Copy
A copy of a spell is a new effect on the stack, not played; a unit that becomes a copy of a card takes that card's name, printed stats, attributes and text. See rules 108.4, 710.1.
Cost
Something a player must pay to do something: to play a card, to apply a mod, or to activate an ability. See rule 111.1.
Cost orb
The part of a card that shows its mana cost. See rule 202.1.
Counterattack
The non-initiative team's attack in a battle phase with two battle rounds. See rule 610.1.
Creature (Obsolete)
The old rules glossary's word for what these rules call a unit. See rule 301.1.
Cube draft
A format for large groups in which players draft decks before the game and then play constructed matches. See rule 902.6.
Damage
What a source deals to a unit or a player: marked on a unit, and lost as life by a player. See rule 112.5.
Damage sub-step
One of the three parts of the combat damage step, taken in order: the Swift sub-step, the normal sub-step and the Sluggish sub-step. See rule 608.2.
Deadly
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit." See rule 802.3.
Debt
A counter a player has, paid off at 1 mana each at the end of that player's resource step. See rule 112.14.
Deck
The face-down pile that cards are drawn from and that packs are dealt from. See rule 401.1.
Defense
The second of a unit's stats: how much damage it can take before it dies. See rules 206.1, 301.4.
Delete
A way for a unit to die: it is removed from play into the bin. See rule 801.5.
Deployment phase
The last phase of each turn, in which players build up their forces for the next. See rule 507.1.
Despawn
What a unit does whenever it leaves play, by any route. See rule 410.2.
Devastating (Obsolete)
Not defined by these rules: an attribute the old rules glossary names without defining it, which no current card prints. See rule 802.1.
Discard
To put a card from a hand into the bin. See rule 801.3.
Dormant
Face down: every resource enters play dormant, and activating it turns it face up (active). See rule 106.3.
Draft step
The step of the planning phase in which, in a live draft, each player combines their hand with their pack and chooses which cards to keep in hand. See rule 503.2.
Draw step
The step of the planning phase in which each player draws 2 cards. See rule 503.1.
Each opponent
Each opponent in the region where the effect happens. See rule 102.2.
Each player
Each player in the region where the effect happens. See rule 102.3.
Effect
Anything on the stack. See rule 700.1.
Electric
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Excess damage from electric sources can be directed to an adjacent unit, recursively." See rule 802.17.
Eliminated
Out of the game: a player whose life total reaches 0 is eliminated. See rule 104.1.
End of turn
A special step after deployment finishes, in which abilities that trigger "at the end of turn" trigger. See rule 508.1.
Enemy
A unit not under your control in the region where the effect is happening. See rule 102.8.
Erase
To take a card out of the game, to the erased pile. See rule 801.6.
Erased pile
The zone where a card goes when an effect erases it. See rules 407.2, 801.6.
Evasive
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Evasive units require two blockers." See rule 802.13.
Excess damage
For Piercing, the damage a source deals to a unit beyond that unit's lethal damage. See rule 802.16a.
Exchange
A word printed in four senses, each read from its card. See rule 801.13.
Expend
To turn a resource sideways for 1 mana, once per turn, to pay a mana cost. See rule 106.5.
Feeble
An attribute: a Feeble unit can't block. See rule 802.12.
Fight
When two units fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other. See rule 801.11.
Fizzle
What an effect does if, as it resolves, it has lost all of its targets: it does nothing. See rule 704.6.
Flying
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units." See rule 802.2.
Formation
The placement of a player's units when they attack or block: an attacking or a defending formation. See rule 602.1.
Free-for-all
A player setup (FFA) in which every player plays for themselves. See rule 903.1.
Full control
A client mode, held with the Control key, in which the client gives a player every stop. See rule D2.7.
Glimpse
Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest. See rule 801.9.
Graft
A modification, marked by the graft symbol, that combines several effects under a single cause. See rule 722.1.
Half-column
The attacking units of one column, or its blocking units, which deal their combat damage together as one source. See rule 608.1c.
Hand
The zone of a player's own cards, which each player has and which is hidden from the other players. See rules 402.1, 402.2.
Haste
A timing keyword: a card with Haste can be played during the haste step as well as during deployment. See rules 803.2, 207.3.
Haste step
The last step of the planning phase, in which players may play only haste cards. See rules 504.1, 504.2.
Hidden simultaneous segment
A part of the turn in which both players act at once and neither sees what the other does until both are done. See rule D1.4.
Host
The card a mod is applied to and becomes part of. See rule 720.6.
Hybrid
A card that belongs to two elements. See rule 105.2.
Initiative
What one player has in each turn; in a 1v1 game the initiative player acts first. See rule 500.3.
Initiative token
The marker of which player has the initiative, passed clockwise when the turn is over; it is not a token. See rules 508.3, 508.4.
Intent card
A card with which players declare attacks in free-for-all, all at the same time. See rule 905.1.
Inverted
An attribute whose reminder text begins "Invert the stat changes of inverted units." See rule 802.8.
Keyword action
A verb that card text uses with a fixed game meaning. See rule 801.1.
Last-known state
What a unit was at the instant it left play. See rule 714.1.
Learn to Play
One learner against the Tutorial Bot in one continuous game, with lessons shown as each rule first matters. See rule D8.1.
Lethal
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Any combat damage from a lethal unit will kill a player." See rule 802.24.
Life
What each player has, starting at 30; a player whose life total reaches 0 is eliminated. See rules 112.1, 104.1.
Live draft
A game mode in which the players share one deck and draft cards from it during the game. See rule 902.1.
Mana cost
The number of resources a player must expend to play a card, shown in its cost orb. See rules 202.1, 111.1a.
Mod
A modification: a card that is applied to another card instead of being played. See rules 305.1, 720.1.
Modular
An attribute whose reminder text begins "You can apply mods to a modular card from your hand and/or bin as it is played." See rules 802.26, 724.1.
Negate
To remove an effect from the stack: a negated effect is removed at once, when the effect that negates it resolves. See rule 704.4.
Non-combat attribute
An attribute printed in purple, such as Burst and Unstable, that describes a card and generally has nothing to do with combat. See rules 803.1, 802.1b.
Noncombat damage
All damage other than combat damage. See rule 112.7.
Nonspell effect
Any effect that is not a spell effect. See rule 700.1b.
Once
The [once] keyword: an ability marked [once] can be activated or triggered only once per turn. See rules 803.4, 109.9.
Open decision
A question the game is waiting on a player to answer, which they must answer, or concede, before taking any other action. See rule D2.1.
Owner
The player whose card it is; a card's owner never changes. See rule 102.4.
Pack
In live draft, each player's face-down pile of 10 cards dealt from the deck, which that player drafts from. See rule 409.1.
Phase
One of the four parts of a turn: the planning, battle, regroup and deployment phases. See rule 500.1.
Piercing
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Excess damage from piercing sources is dealt to the recipient's controller." See rule 802.16.
Pips
The element marks with a card's cost, which are its affinity requirement and not part of its cost. See rule 202.2.
Planning phase
The first phase of the turn, in which players prepare for the turn ahead. See rule 501.1.
Play
The zone of the units, resources and tokens on the table. See rule 404.1.
Playing a card
What is done to units and spells, from whatever zone: meeting the card's affinity requirement, paying its mana cost and selecting its targets. See rules 701.1, 702.1.
Poisonous
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Poisonous sources damage units in the form of -1/-1 counters." See rule 802.18.
Power
The first of a unit's stats: how much damage it deals in combat. See rules 206.1, 301.3.
Powerful
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Powerful sources deal double damage." See rule 802.10.
Prevention effect
An effect that prevents damage that would be dealt; it is not a replacement effect. See rules 708.11, 112.11.
Priority
The ability to take game actions such as playing cards or activating abilities. See rule 703.2.
Priority window
A sequence in which the players (or teams) each receive priority in order. See rule 703.3.
Prismite
A resource with no element, which gives no affinity. See rule 106.8.
Prophecy
A keyword printed on a card's banner as a cost and a condition. See rule 803.7.
Prophesy
To pay the cost on a card's prophecy banner and put it into the cache with its prophecy attached. See rule 801.14.
Pure
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes." See rule 802.25.
Ranged (Obsolete)
Not defined by these rules: the 2023 Rulebook's attribute that dealt combat damage first and could block fliers, which no current card prints. See rules 802.4, 802.2.
Reaping
An attribute whose reminder text begins "When a reaping source kills one or more units, draw a card." See rule 802.21.
Recall
To put a card into a hand. See rule 801.7.
Recap
The playback each player is shown of what the other did in the haste step or in deployment. See rule D5.1.
Recycle
To put a card on the bottom of the deck, past the deck's mark, into the recycle pile. See rules 801.10, 408.1.
Recycle pile
The cards past the deck's mark, where a card put on the bottom of the deck goes. See rule 408.2.
Refresh
The first step of the planning phase, in which each player's expended resources refresh. See rules 501.2a, 106.5.
Region
Where all gameplay takes place; there is one region for each player. See rule 601.1.
Regroup
The global step, once battle has ended in every region, that resets the game between battles. See rule 506.1.
Reminder text
Italic text that restates what an attribute or keyword does. See rule 205.2.
Replacement effect
An ability that changes an event as it happens, written "If … instead". See rule 708.1.
Resonant
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Whenever a resonant source deals damage to a unit, it deals that much damage to that unit's controller." See rule 802.19.
Resource
A source of mana, which a player needs to play cards. See rule 106.1.
Resource step
The step of the planning phase in which players create and activate resources. See rule 502.1.
Rockfall
Rockfall N means: each player chooses one of their units, and the source of the rockfall deals N damage to each chosen unit. See rule 801.12.
Rot
A counter a player has, which deals that player damage equal to it at the start of each deployment phase. See rule 112.13.
Sacrifice
For a player to choose a unit they control and put it into their bin. See rule 801.4.
Safe point
A moment at which the game makes state checks, such as the end of every action. See rules 713.3, 713.1.
Shard
A resource of its own kind, which pays one generic mana once activated. See rule 106.9.
Side-block
A defending unit placed blocking where no attacker is. See rule 606.4.
Single Card Duel
A variant of constructed in which each player picks a single card and their deck is 30 copies of it. See rules 901.8, D8.2.
Skirmish (Obsolete)
The old rules glossary's name for the place where attackers meet defenders, one per player; the current term is region. See rule 601.1.
Sluggish
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Sluggish units deal combat damage last." See rule 802.5.
Sneaky
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Sneaky units can't be blocked if attacking alone." See rule 802.14.
Source
The thing that deals damage. See rule 112.6.
Spell
A card type that provides a one-time effect. See rules 302.1, 300.1.
Spell effect
An effect that is a spell: a spell, a spell unit or a spell token on the stack. See rule 700.1a.
Spell token
A spell that an effect creates directly into play, which its controller may cast from play. See rules 304.11, 108.2.
Spell unit
A card that is both a spell and a unit. See rule 303.1.
Stack
The zone where cards being played, and abilities, wait to resolve, the last one put there resolving first. See rules 406.1, 703.1.
Standing pass
Pass through stack or Pass all: a promise the client keeps on a player's behalf in later windows. See rule D2.2.
State check
A check the game itself makes at safe points, in which every unit that should be dead dies. See rule 713.1.
Static ability
An ability that states a change its card continuously makes to the game for as long as the card is in play. See rules 707.1, 109.4.
Stats
A unit's two numbers, printed power/defense. See rule 206.1.
Strip
An effect that makes a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both. See rule 712.1.
Subtype
A word of the type line other than its markers and its card type, such as Whale. See rule 204.3.
Swift
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Swift units deal combat damage first." See rule 802.4.
Target
Something a card or ability chooses, with the word "target", to receive its actions. See rule 110.1.
Team game
A player setup in which two teams play against each other, 2v2 or 3v3. See rule 904.1.
Thieving
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Whenever a thieving source deals combat damage to an opponent, draw a card." See rule 802.20.
Timestamp
When an effect began to apply. See rule 113.2.
Timing icon
An icon in the top right corner of a card that changes when, and how, the card can be played. See rule 207.1.
Token
A unit or a spell that an effect creates directly into play; a token is not a card. See rules 108.2, 304.2.
Tough
An attribute: a Tough unit's defense is doubled. See rule 802.6.
Transform
To turn a card in play to its other face up; it stays the same unit and does not leave play. See rule 108.3.
Trash
What happens to a card that enters a bin from any zone except the stack. See rule 801.2.
Triggered ability
An ability that happens when something else takes place. See rule 706.1.
Turn
The global cycle of four phases that every player goes through together. See rules 500.1, 100.2.
Type line
The line of a card that describes what the card is. See rule 204.1.
Unaware
An attribute: an Unaware card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all stat changes: each is read at the stats printed on it. See rule 802.9.
Unit
A card type that, once it enters play, stays there until something removes it; units attack and defend. See rules 301.1, 300.1.
Unit token
A unit that an effect creates, whether or not the effect calls it a token. See rules 304.4, 304.9.
Unstable
A non-combat attribute: an Unstable card that would enter a bin from an active zone is erased instead. See rule 803.8.
Virus
A timing icon: a Virus card can also be applied as an augment from the hand during battle. See rule 723.1.
Vulnerable
An attribute: a Vulnerable unit is dealt double the damage that would be dealt to it. See rule 802.11.
X
A number that the card defines. See rule 107.1.
You
On a card, the controller of the effect. See rule 102.6.
Zone
One of the places a card can be: the deck, the hand, the cache, play, the bin, the stack, the erased pile, the recycle pile and the pack. See rule 400.1.

Keyed by rule key. A number never moves, so a rule is new, removed or renamed; text changes to a rule are not listed yet.

Annex D — Digital Play Conventions

These are the conventions of this digital client: how it times, shows and confirms the game, where a table of players would simply agree. They are not rules of Algomancy. Where a convention here and a rule in the main document both speak to the game itself, the main document governs. Where they concern only how the client presents, times or confirms play, this annex governs.

D1. General and Precedence

D1.1. The pacing and concurrency conventions in this annex are not rules changes: none of them changes what is legal. See rules D3, D3.3, D3.4b.

D1.2b The game takes an action for a player only where the battle leaves them nothing to decide: an attacker with no unit able to attack has the empty attack declared for them; a lone counterattacker has its one-unit formation declared, its sent spell tokens riding (see rule D1.2c); and a defender with no unit in the battle region, or facing an attack with no attacking unit left and unable to send a counterattacker, has the empty block declared for them. These forced actions are logged like any other. A player holding full control is not forced: the window is left to them. See rules 610, D1.2c, D1.2f, D1.2e, D2.7.

Example: In round 2 the lone counterattacker is destroyed before blocks: the initiative player's empty block is declared for them, though they have a unit in the region.

D1.2c In round 2, a counterattack pool that holds exactly one unit able to attack declares the one-unit formation by itself, with every spell token sent with it riding along: the unit and its tokens must attack, and one unit has only one shape. See rule 610.

D1.2d When all of one player's simultaneously queued triggers are identical (the same card, the same ability and the same composed parts), the player is not asked to order them. Example: Three allies spawn at once beside Flourishing Flora: its three identical triggers go on the stack without the player being asked to order them.

D1.2i When a player chooses the order of replacement effects (see rule 708.4a), each choice is the unit whose effect it is: the player answers by clicking that unit on the board, the choices are not also buttons in the prompt bar, and the prompt says what is being chosen. A question raised by combat damage or by rot is asked before any of that damage or rot is dealt. The other player sees that a question is open, but not the question; while the rot question is open at the start of deployment, the other player cannot deploy.

Example: Two Oorblaks: the prompt asks which Oorblak takes the damage first, and clicking the second Oorblak chooses it.

Example: The attacker sees that the defender is being asked, but not the question.

Example: Two Skittering Blights at the start of deployment: the rot question is answered on the board, and the other player can deploy only once it is answered.

Example: A Poisonous blocker and two Counter Thieves: the question comes before any of the combat damage is dealt.

D1.5. Where the printed rules have the initiative player take the resource step and the haste step first, and the initiative team deploy first (rules 501.4 and rule 507.3), this client runs those steps for both players at once, each hidden from the other (rule D1.4). The non-initiative player neither waits for the initiative player nor sees what they did before acting. This is a house rule of the client. See rules 501, 507, D1.4.

Example: The non-initiative player is offered plays at once in deployment, and can finish deploying while the initiative player is still acting.

D2.9. This client does not keep priority for a player who acts unless they ask: in battle, once their action is on the stack, priority goes to the opponent.   • Key annexd.undo.hidden-step.opponent

D4.1b An undo cannot go back past what the step itself did as it began, such as a payment or an ability that happens at the start of the step. A player's own undo, in any step, never takes back an agreed edit (see rule D4.5), and takes back an action from before one only if the edit would mean exactly the same afterwards. It never goes back past the point an agreed rewind returned the game to: only another agreed rewind can.

Example: An undo stops at what the step did as it began: the answer to a start-of-deployment trigger cannot be taken back.

Example: After an agreed rewind of one action in planning, the player cannot undo, alone, the action before it.

Example: After an agreed fix in planning names a card by its place in the hand, the player cannot undo the earlier recycle that would put a different card there, while the other player may still undo a move the fix does not depend on.

Sources and verification
Engine onlyConfirmedverified in round 4 · verifier ran 3 tests, all passed · 3 gate test files

  • Example tests 434-cr-digital-1.test.ts::cr:annexd.undo.hidden-step.floor — an undo stops at what the step did as it began: the answer to a start-of-deployment trigger cannot be taken back, 485-agreed-fix-rooms.test.ts::§2 the per-seat undo cannot walk back past an agreed fix, 485-agreed-fix-rooms.test.ts::§7 in the step, an undo passes a fix only when the fix would mean the same
  • Key annexd.undo.hidden-step.floor

D4.1c One player cannot undo actions taken in battle, except the steps of a cast that has not yet gone on the stack (see rule D4.2); both players together may take them back with an agreed rewind (see rule D4.5d). For that reason, in battle, an activated ability whose cost spends life, debt or the unit itself, with no choice to make before that cost is paid, asks for confirmation. While it asks, only a second click on the same unit, the Yes button or Enter confirms; No and Escape cancel; every other input does nothing. An ability whose cost asks which card to discard or which other unit to sacrifice does not ask for confirmation: choosing what to pay is the question. In deployment such an ability activates on the click, and undo is the safety net. See rule D7.

Example: Cadaverous Cultivator ("[Battle] Discard a card: …") raises no confirmation: the click activates it, and the game asks which card to discard.

Example: While the confirmation is up, clicking a card in hand plays nothing.

In a Single Card Duel nothing locks, since every card in the deck is the same. See rule D8.

D4.5a An edit is one of: setting a player's life total, to a whole number from 1 to 999; a player drawing from 1 to 10 cards off the top of their deck; moving one of the proposer's own cards from their hand, bin or cache to their hand, bin or cache, or to the top or bottom of their deck; or taking a unit off the board to its controller's hand, bin or the bottom of their deck. A token taken off the board is simply gone.

Example: A fix cannot set a life total to 0, nor move a card that is no longer where the proposer saw it.

See rule 405.4.

Example: Rotling does not hear a card that a fix takes out of the bin.

D4.5d A rewind takes the game back to one of: just before the proposing player's own last action, even when more than five actions came after it; just before any of the last five actions, counting only actions a player took (an action the game took for a player is neither counted nor a place to stop); the start of the current step; or the start of the step before. Each option names, in the proposing player's words, what it takes back. Inside a hidden step, a point within the step is offered only if it takes back none of the other player's hidden actions there (their public ones, such as finishing the step, may be taken back); the start of the step may take back the other player's hidden actions too. The actions taken back are removed from the game, as if they had not been taken. See rule D1.2b.

Sources and verification Partial
Owner callPartialverified in round 4 · verifier ran 9 tests (4 probes it wrote), all passed · 3 gate test files

Verifier: Almost all of it holds and is demonstrated (bound tests plus probes zz-U23-1..3). One clause fails: 'their public ones, such as finishing the step, may be taken back'. Finishing the step is public only in planning and deployment (PUBLIC_IN_HIDDEN = donePlanning, doneDeploying, amend). In the haste step the done-flag is hidden (view.ts redacts hasteDone), so no in-step cut over the other player's doneHaste is offered. Suggested fix: 'such as being done planning or done deploying'. Smaller points: the own-last-action option looks back only 80 logged actions (FIX_REWIND_WINDOW), and an agreed edit counts among the five. Basis: 'owner' covers only the five-actions and step-start options; the rest is server code plus tests, so the honest basis is mixed (owner + engine), which this pipeline cannot express because sources.engine takes only client/engine/src symbols. Divergence filed under bugs: the 'start of the step before' option can land on a forced action and then arrive at the start of the current step.

  • Owner call adopted 2026-10-16 (report round 2026-10-16 b, BL-46 (in session)): Rewinding a whole step or two seems fine to me. Either say "up to 5 actions" or "restart this step"

D4.5e A proposal states the fix and the proposer's reason, which is required. It lapses after 60 seconds, or as soon as any action lands, and the proposer may withdraw it. Only the other player can accept it; after a decline the proposer must wait 15 seconds before proposing again. The proposer's reason is filed as a bug report. Fixes made one after another, with no game action between them, are one run and file one report, with every fix's reason in order; the run is filed when it ends, for instance when the next game action lands, and a server restart before then does not lose it. See rule D3.2.

D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps

D6.1. The resource step, the haste step and deployment are hidden simultaneous steps. Inside one, both players act at the same time, and neither is shown what the other does until the step ends. The end of the step is the reveal: everything the other player did in the step is shown then. At the end of the haste step and of deployment it is played back in the recap. See rule D6.2.

Example: During deployment, nothing a player does in their region reaches the other player until deployment ends.

D6.4. Outside a hidden simultaneous step, that a player owes an answer to a question is public, and so is the card it comes from when that card is already in view. What the question is is not: its prompt, its options, its candidate targets and its kind are shown only to the player who must answer. Inside a hidden simultaneous step, not even the fact that the other player owes an answer is shown.

Example: The attacker's Tempest Wrangler makes them choose an {Alluring} target. The defender's bar reads "Waiting for Rashi (Tempest Wrangler)" and names neither the prompt nor the candidate.

D6.5a When an effect lets a player look at another player's hand, the cards are shown to the looker only: the client keeps them in the looker's note-taking strip, and no log line names them to anyone else (where a card's log line names them, it goes to the looker alone). D6.18. An arrow from an effect to its target is aimed at the exact centre of the target. Discrepancy report

Every place where the sources disagree, the register contradicts itself, or a rule rests only on the engine or on an owner call. Each quote is checked to be verbatim. Only the first tier needs a decision.

Questions for the owner 6

D-U06-9 Other rule 305.6

Eldritch Dreamtender, Cthyrian Rector and Void Mandible print "sacrifice me. If you do, …" as effect text, with no bracket. The owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“"Sacrifice me" is a CAST COST…”) reads the sacrifice as a cost paid as the ability goes on the stack, and says so.

Resolution: Settled by printed text, read literally: Eldritch Dreamtender, Cthyrian Rector and Void Mandible print "sacrifice me. If you do, …" as effect text after a "When …" trigger condition, with no cost brackets, so the sacrifice is a step of the effect, carried out as the ability resolves; a player may respond while the unit is still in play, and if it has gone by then, "If you do" fails. The sacrifice stays mandatory (no "may"; Void Mandible prints "(This is not optional.)"). The owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“"Sacrifice me" is a CAST COST…”) reads the prose as a bracketed cost on the owner's understanding that the unit "needs to be sacrificed for its ability to go on the stack", and says itself that the card has no brackets; print outranks it. The designer says the same of Eldritch Dreamtender (RQ 1363535826436493614): if the opponent kills it with the trigger on the stack, it cannot be sacrificed and nothing is discarded; the owner accepted that reading on 2026-10-21. Document fix: done 2026-10-10 (rule 111.8 states print). Engine fix: done 2026-10-21 (CT-264, report #259; F-U04-5 and F-U04-6 closed): the sacrifice is made as the trigger resolves, and 515 drives all three cards.
